live_web_research.page_text: [2610.07707] AgentMemGate: Addressing Speculation Contamination in Conversational Assistant Memory Skip to main content Search arXiv Press Enter to search · Advanced search --> Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence arXiv:2610.07707 (cs) [Submitted on 6 Oct 2026] Title: AgentMemGate: Addressing Speculation Contamination in Conversational Assistant Memory Authors: Chirag Sharma , Benjamin Fowlersmith , Karime Maamari View a PDF of the paper titled AgentMemGate: Addressing Speculation Contamination in Conversational Assistant Memory, by Chirag Sharma and 2 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Conversational AI assistants with long-term memory extract facts from user messages into a store consulted in later conversations. A stated plan can enter that store as fact: a user who might move to Seattle may be recorded as already living there. We call this speculation contamination. Final-state memory benchmarks miss this error because they do not probe intermediate state and include few unresolved speculations. We present AgentMemGate, a write-time gate for profile-store memory that classifies extracted statements as speculation, completed event, correction, or other. Speculations remain outside memory, with conditions governing later promotion or deletion. We also contribute a dataset of multi-session conversations in which plans are confirmed, abandoned, or left unresolved. On our 147-conversation held-out set, Mem0 and Graphiti assert unresolved plans as current state for 35.2% and 27.3% of pending plans. On the core benchmark, AgentMemGate eliminates all observed contamination relative to the identical ungated pipeline (87.5% to zero for the most exposed extraction style) and raises task accuracy from 65% to 95%. On the harder held-out set, gated contamination is 3.4% to 5.7% and task accuracy rises by 9 to 13 percentage points. Our analysis identifies field matching as the main remaining bottleneck: realistic speculations often match no profile field and never reach the gate. We release our datasets, prompts, and evaluation code. selected_records.title: AgentMemGate: Addressing Speculation Contamination in Conversational Assistant Memory

article.body:
AgentMemGate filters speculation before it enters assistant memory

AgentMemGate is a write-time gate for profile-store memory in conversational AI systems. It targets pipelines that extract user statements for later conversations. The gate classifies statements as speculation, completed event, correction or other; speculative statements stay out of memory, with conditions for later promotion or deletion.

In the paper’s core benchmark, the gated pipeline reduced observed contamination from 87.5% to zero for the most exposed extraction style, compared with the same pipeline without the gate. On a harder held-out set, contamination remained at 3.4%–5.7%; field matching often prevented speculations from reaching the gate. This is a research result, not evidence of a deployed product. The paper reports releasing datasets, prompts and evaluation code. Product availability not specified.
